1771.title: The flood of 1771, an estimate, on the town of about 1788
1771.caption: Water at about 38 ft above sea level (NAVD88) at the City Locks, derived from a 1771 stage of 38 ft on the old gauge near Mayo's Bridge (the Corps, from diaries); other accounts give 30 ft and 45 ft on unstated bases; ±3 ft is our judgment. Hatched: up to 41 ft.
notes: {floodAcres} acres under water off the channel; buildings in the water: {floodShownInWater} of the {floodShown} shown ({floodShownDepthMedianFt} ft median, {floodShownDepthMaxFt} ft deepest).
Bathtub fill, not a flood model, on today's ground; the town of 1788 as the downtown history draws it: few of its buildings are known. FINAL DRAFT rc3.

unknown.note: Not known: the earthen levee is not mapped
unknown.about: rc2 (Chris, November 25, 2026, 12:27): land the with-wall fill reaches only because the levee is not in our data. The first line continues the south wall's east tie-in south along the lidar ridge by I-95 past the frame; the second runs from the wall's east end along the river's south edge, just off the shore, past the frame (the levee could stand anywhere between I-95 and the bank). Land flooded with the wall but dry with both lines as walls is drawn as not known. The levee's course is given as along the west side of I-95, then south and west to Goodes Street (City FloodKit; floodwall.md), and WRDA 1986 sec. 401 says the project shall include flood protection for the wastewater plant; neither puts it on our map, so both courses are closed.

1996-nowall.title: Hurricane Fran, September 1996, against the new floodwall
1996-nowall.caption: Water at 22.7 ft above sea level (NAVD88) at the City Locks, perhaps 1 ft more (hatched), about 24.0 ft at the Mayo Bridge. Weather service crest record.
notes: {floodAcres} acres under water off the channel; {floodBuildingsInWater} of the {buildings} buildings shown stand in it ({floodDepthAtBuildingsMedianFt} ft median, {floodDepthAtBuildingsMaxFt} ft deepest).

A bathtub fill on today's ground, not a flood model. Buildings: standing today by year built, traced from the 1886 to 1952 fire-insurance maps, or seen on aerial photographs of 1974, 1999, 2002, 2017 and 2021. Grey, dashed roof edge: {periodUnconfirmed} buildings on an earlier map or photograph but not ascertained for this year. Wall top: the 41 ft overtopping stage, not surveyed. Left out: {outbuildingsHidden} such outbuildings (under 60 m², off the street, 60 m from the water). WORKING DRAFT d3.

markers.key: 1  17th Street Market: where most of the water came together (Washington Post).
2  Havana '59, 16 N. 17th St.: water 13 ft up the dining-room wall, by the owner's account (Washington Post).
3  Bottoms Up Pizza, 1700 Dock St.: 6 ft 2 in inside, over a 3 ft step, about 9 ft above the street (owner, NBC12).
4  15th and Main: "rapids" in the street (a witness).
5  Main Street Station: escaped damage (Washington Post).

notes: Rain, not the James: 6 to 12 in in eight hours; the river stayed low and the wall's gates stood open. Depths are reports, not surveys; the edge is an estimate.
1 17th Street Market, where most water converged · 2 Havana '59, 13 ft up the wall · 3 Bottoms Up, about 9 ft · 4 15th and Main, "rapids" · 5 Main Street Station, which escaped damage.

The ground lets still water out at 19 to 22 ft; it stood higher because it came faster than it could leave. Grey, dashed roof edge: {periodUnconfirmed} buildings on an earlier map or photograph but not ascertained for this year. Left out: {outbuildingsHidden} such outbuildings (under 60 m², off the street, 60 m from the water). WORKING DRAFT d3.
